title: 2007 AMC 10B Problem 11
statement: A circle passes through the three vertices of an isosceles triangle that has two sides of length \(3\) and a base of length \(2.\) What is the area of this circle?

solutions.text:
The triangle has sides \(3,\) \(3,\) and \(2.\) Its area is \(\dfrac12\cdot 2\cdot\sqrt{3^2-1^2}=2\sqrt2.\)

The circumradius is \(R=\dfrac{abc}{4K}\) \(=\dfrac{3\cdot 3\cdot 2}{4\cdot 2\sqrt2}\) \(=\dfrac{9}{4\sqrt2}\) \(=\dfrac{9\sqrt2}{8}.\)

The area of the circle is \(\pi R^2=\pi\cdot\dfrac{81\cdot 2}{64}=\dfrac{81}{32}\pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Use the circumradius formula \(R=\dfrac{abc}{4K},\) where \(K\) is the triangle’s area
The sides are \(3,\) \(3,\) and \(2;\) find the area from the base and height, then compute \(R\)
